## The task

Load the four standards documents and three of the empirical papers from the [source shelf](../ai.qmd#the-source-shelf) into a single grounded workspace (NotebookLM, a Claude Project, or a ChatGPT project — any tool that lets you attach sources).

Ask it: *"What percentage of large projects fail, according to the sources I gave you?"* Then ask the same question in a fresh chat **with no sources attached**.

**Deliverable.** One page: both answers side by side, the specific differences, and — this is the graded part — a claim the ungrounded model made that is *not supported by any source on the shelf*, with the source that contradicts it.

## Tutor prompt for this week

Run this before you read the notes, and again after.

```text
Be my tutor on what "project success" means and why it's contested. Ask me
one question at a time. Don't lecture. Start by making me define success,
then attack my definition. Push until I admit it's multidimensional, then
make me name the dimensions myself.
```

## The weekly loop

This lab is step 4–6 of the loop. The whole cycle:

```text
1. TUTOR (diagnostic)  — 10 min — what do I already wrongly believe?
2. Read the module     — 20 min — notes + one primary source
3. TUTOR (voice)       — 20 min — one question at a time, no lecturing
4. Write something     — 15 min — a plan, an argument, a worked problem
5. EDITOR              — 10 min — attack what I wrote
6. ROOMMATE            —  5 min — where else does this structure appear?
7. TUTOR (retrieval)   —  5 min — mixed questions from all prior weeks
```

Steps 4 and 5 do the work. A loop that stops after step 3 feels productive and mostly isn't.

## Submission

Upload to Blackboard as a single PDF. Include your prompts. Label every AI-produced element and attach the verification, per the [AI policy](../syllabus.qmd#artificial-intelligence-policy).
